title: Sonoko's Red Handkerchief
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Sonoko, Professor Agasa, investigating Officer Yamamura) omitted by convention, matching ep011. Kyougoku Makoto (Sonoko's boyfriend) is also omitted: his only on-screen actions (fighting off gang members) target exclusively omitted cast members (Ran, Sonoko) and don't touch the murder-mystery graph (victim, culprit, evidence, motive). No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep457-458_sonokos_red_handkerchief.json) got the culprit right (Watanuki Tatsuzou) but its clue c1 ('victim's name misread as a date, explaining why police couldn't find him on a crew list') garbles the actual dying-message trick: the transcript's date/kanji pun (calendar entry for April 1st, unusually read 'Watanuki') is the dying message identifying the KILLER's surname, not an explanation of the victim's absence from a crew list -- that's a separate, never-fully-resolved thread in the transcript (the production company said it had no Assistant Director named Hozumi; a part-timer's staff-list copy had mixed-up dates, and the scene leaves it ambiguous whether that staffer or Hozumi himself was mistaken/lying). The old file also omitted the backstory murder entirely (the gang-leadership killing that led to the original burial + handkerchief), added here as its own victim node. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Hozumi's planner has blood smeared specifically over the April 1st entry; the kanji for "April 1st" is an unusual reading of the surname "Watanuki" -- a dying message naming the killer, not a random smear.

Hozumi's own name in his planner and the guestbook signature he dictated are both in katakana; his surname's kanji ("August 1st") is unusually read "Hozumi", explaining his personal habit -- the foreigner/old-man katakana theories were coincidental misdirection.

The real grave tree is over 500 meters from the rock used in the drama's last scene, which the film crew deliberately avoided shooting near to keep both red handkerchiefs out of frame -- explaining why Watanuki, searching only near the rock, never found his own marker.
